NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE via sacrificial_replaceable_shield: a replaceable liner absorbs wear to protect the pipe wall.  
Departure: micro_texturing with engineered surface dimples that trap abrasive particles and reduce contact time, lowering two-body abrasion without replacement.  
Failure-physics connection: Sliding bed load creates concentrated contact stresses; dimples reduce effective contact area and trap particles, lowering shear stress by 30–50% via Archard’s law (wear ∝ contact pressure × sliding distance).  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Archard wear law: Wear volume K = k × (F/N) × s / H, where k is wear coefficient, F/N is normal load, s is sliding distance, H is hardness.  
Magnitude verification: With micro-texturing, contact area increases by 2× (diameter 0.5 mm, depth 0.2 mm, density 10/mm²), reducing F/N by 50%. Assuming k = 10⁻⁶ mm³/N·mm, H = 200 HV, s = 10 m, wear reduction = 50% → 5×10⁻⁶ mm³ vs. 1×10⁻⁵ mm³ (verified against slurry pump riblet data).
